batchName: Middle Republic: The Gracchi (133-121 BCE) - Medium Batch 2

questions.question: One of the triumphs celebrated by the Gracchi's father honoured him for what achievement?
options: Bringing twenty years of peace to Spain
Clearing the seas of Cilician pirates
questions.explanation: The elder Tiberius was honoured for pacifying Spain. That reputation later made the Numantines trust his son.
questions.sourceQuote: One honoured him for bringing twenty years of peace to Spain.

questions.question: How did Opimius win his trial for executing citizens without appeal?
options: He claimed Gaius had attacked first
He proved the dead men were not citizens
He fled into exile before the verdict
He cited the Senate's emergency decree
questions.explanation: Ironically, Opimius was prosecuted under Gaius's own law. His acquittal gave Senate emergency decrees new legitimacy.
questions.sourceQuote: Prosecuted under Gaius's own law against executing citizens without appeal, Opimius won by pointing to the Senate's emergency decree, giving such decrees new legitimacy.

questions.question: Gaius Gracchus was accused of helping a revolt in 125 BC at which Latin town?
questions.explanation: Gaius cleared himself of the charge and went on to be elected tribune for 123 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: He was later accused of helping a revolt in 125 BC at Fregellae, a Latin town south-east of Rome, but cleared himself and was elected tribune for 123 BC.

questions.question: Which benefits did Tiberius claim his land law would bring? (select all that apply)
options: Slowing the drift of country people into the city
More men qualifying for army service
questions.explanation: Tiberius linked land ownership to poverty, urban migration and military recruitment. He also blamed rich landowners for a supposed decline in Rome's population.
questions.sourceQuote: He argued that this would help the poor, slow the drift of country people into the city, and increase the number of men who owned enough property to qualify for army service.

questions.question: What did an inscription carved one night say about Opimius's new temple?
options: It was built on the Gracchi's graves
It was paid for with Pergamene gold
It was the product of mad discord
It was the work of a tyrant
questions.explanation: The graffiti read: 'A work of mad discord produces a temple of Concord.' It showed that not everyone accepted the official story of restored harmony.
questions.sourceQuote: One night someone carved an inscription: "A work of mad discord produces a temple of Concord."

questions.question: Why did Scipio Nasica draw his toga over his head as he led the attack on Tiberius?
options: To present the attack as a religious rite
To shield his head from stones
To hide his face from the voters
To show mourning for the Republic
To show he carried no weapon
questions.explanation: Priests covered their heads at sacrifices, so Nasica framed the killing as a rite to rid Rome of a would-be tyrant.
questions.sourceQuote: Drawing his toga over his head, as a priest did at a sacrifice, he led a mob to the voting place, framing the attack as a religious rite to rid Rome of a would-be tyrant.

questions.question: After 129 BC, which group's protests slowed the work of the land commission?
questions.explanation: The allies said the commissioners were seizing land they had long used, which they saw as their reward for loyalty.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome's Italian allies, the peoples of Italy who fought alongside Rome but lacked citizenship, protested that the commissioners were seizing land they had long used.

questions.question: In which region of Italy did Gaius Gracchus distribute land after renewing his brother's land law?
questions.explanation: Gaius handed out land in Apulia, in Italy's south-east. Realising Italy lacked enough land, he also planned colonies.
questions.sourceQuote: He also renewed his brother's land law and distributed land in Apulia, the south-eastern region of Italy.

questions.question: Which episode shows Cornelia's lasting influence over her son Gaius?
options: She wrote his most famous speeches
He dropped one of his own bills at her request
She chose his fellow tribunes for him
She persuaded him to seize the Aventine
He named his Carthage colony in her honour
questions.explanation: Years after raising her children, Cornelia could still persuade Gaius to abandon a bill. She had devoted herself to their education after her husband died.
questions.sourceQuote: Her influence lasted: years later, Gaius dropped one of his own bills because Cornelia asked him to.

questions.question: What did the equestrians gain from Gaius Gracchus's laws? (select all that apply)
options: Tax-collecting contracts in the province of Asia
Seats on juries trying corrupt officials
questions.explanation: Gaius courted these wealthy non-senators with tax contracts and jury seats. An unintended result was that their tax companies came to exploit the provinces.
questions.sourceQuote: They received tax-collecting contracts in the province of Asia and seats on the juries that tried corrupt officials.
